content: 1. Both darifenacin and diphenhydramine increase sedation and reduce cholinergic effects or transmission. Co-administration may lead to additive psychomotor impairment and daytime dysfunction. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 2. Diphenhydramine enhances the effects of daxibotulinumtoxinA through pharmacodynamic synergy. This interaction may result in excessive neuromuscular weakness and heightened systemic anticholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Co-administration of desflurane and diphenhydramine increases sedation. Patients should be monitored carefully, and therapy adjusted as needed. 4. Diphenhydramine increases the levels or effects of desipramine by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Both drugs also increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Diphenhydramine and desloratadine both increase sedation. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 6. Diphenhydramine and deutetrabenazine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Diphenhydramine and dexchlorpheniramine both increase sedation. Patients should be monitored carefully. 8. Diphenhydramine increases sedation, while dexfenfluramine decreases it. The overall effect of this interaction is unclear, so caution is advised. 9. Diphenhydramine and dexmedetomidine both increase sedation. Therapy should be adjusted, and patients monitored closely. 10. Diphenhydramine increases sedation, while dexmethylphenidate decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear, so use caution and monitor. 11. Diphenhydramine increases sedation, while dextroamphetamine decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear, so use caution and monitor. 12. Diphenhydramine and dextromoramide both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Diphenhydramine and diamorphine both increase sedation. Therapy should be adjusted, and patients monitored closely. 14. Diphenhydramine and diazepam both increase sedation. Co-administration may potentiate CNS-depressant effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Diphenhydramine decreases the levels of droperidol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption and through pharmacodynamic antagonism. However, droperidol increases the effects of diphenhydramine via pharmacodynamic synergy. Additive anticholinergic effects and possible hypoglycemia may occur. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Diphenhydramine increases the levels or effects of duloxetine by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy should be adjusted, and patients monitored closely. 17. Diphenhydramine decreases the effects of hyaluronidase by rendering tissues partially resistant to its action. Patients may require larger amounts of hyaluronidase for equivalent dispersing effects. Use caution and monitor. 18. Diphenhydramine increases the levels or effects of hydrocodone by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Both drugs increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Diphenhydramine and hydroxyzine both increase sedation. Therapy should be adjusted, and patients monitored closely. 20. Diphenhydramine and hyoscyamine both decrease cholinergic effects or transmission. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Diphenhydramine increases the levels or effects of iloperidone by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Both drugs increase sedation. Diphenhydramine also decreases iloperidone levels through gastrointestinal absorption inhibition and pharmacodynamic antagonism. Additive anticholinergic effects and possible hypoglycemia may occur. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Diphenhydramine increases the effects of incobotulinumtoxinA through pharmacodynamic synergy. This interaction may result in excessive neuromuscular weakness and heightened systemic anticholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Diphenhydramine increases the levels or effects of imipramine by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Both drugs decrease cholinergic effects and increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Diphenhydramine increases the effects of letibotulinumtoxinA through pharmacodynamic synergy. This interaction may result in excessive neuromuscular weakness and heightened systemic anticholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Diphenhydramine and levetiracetam both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Diphenhydramine and levocetirizine both increase sedation. Therapy should be adjusted, and patients monitored closely. 27. Diphenhydramine increases the effects of haloperidol by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. However, it decreases haloperidol levels through gastrointestinal absorption inhibition and pharmacodynamic antagonism. Haloperidol increases the effects of diphenhydramine via pharmacodynamic synergy. Additive anticholinergic effects and possible hypoglycemia may occur. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Diphenhydramine increases the effects of fentanyl through pharmacodynamic synergy. Co-administration may result in serious, life-threatening respiratory depression. Use the lowest dose possible and monitor for respiratory depression and sedation. 29. Diphenhydramine and gabapentin both increase sedation. Co-administration of CNS depressants can result in serious, life-threatening respiratory depression. Use the lowest dose possible and monitor closely. 30. Diphenhydramine and glycopyrrolate both decrease cholinergic effects or transmission. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Diphenhydramine increases the effects of kava through pharmacodynamic synergy. This interaction may enhance CNS depression. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Diphenhydramine and ketamine both increase sedation. Therapy should be adjusted, and patients monitored closely. 33. Diphenhydramine and lasmiditan both increase sedation. Co-administration with other CNS depressants, including alcohol, has not been evaluated in clinical studies. Lasmiditan may cause sedation and other cognitive or neuropsychiatric adverse reactions. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Diphenhydramine increases the effects of lemborexant through sedation. Dosage adjustment may be necessary if lemborexant is co-administered with other CNS depressants due to potentially additive effects. Use caution and monitor closely.
